messages:
samir: FYI customer AcmeApp hitting the Console — streaming metrics (TTFT + tokens/sec) show gaps and some negative tokens/sec values starting ~03:15 UTC. They're on Dedicated (nyc-1). Screenshot attached. Can we triage?

support-jen: Ack. Customer id 8467. They say their UI shows '—' for TTFT on some streams and negative tokens/sec on others. Any recent deploys to ingest/metrics? @eng-runtime-li

eng-runtime-li: I didn't push any runtime changes last night. Will dig. Can you paste a trace_id or a link to the failing chart? Also, is this only in Console or also raw /metrics?

samir: Trace: trace_0a9f3c. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/streams/8467/trace_0a9f3c. They reported it on both the per-request chart and the streaming dashboard.

support-jen: Repro steps from customer: 1) start streaming session, 2) send some short messages, 3) stop. TTFT sometimes blank; tokens/sec shows -234 or -5.3k on some rows.

eng-runtime-li: Okay thanks. Initial theory: aggregator is computing tokens/sec = tokens / (end_ts - start_ts). If start_ts > end_ts (clock skew or bad event ordering) that yields negative durations -> negative tokens/sec.

ops-maya: We had a restart on ingest-consumer at 02:58 UTC due to a high-file-descriptor alert. Could have caused reordering of buffered events. Kafka lag spiked briefly.

eng-runtime-li: Can you run this quick check on the ingest node?

```
# check for out-of-order timestamps in recent window
psql -c "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM streaming_events WHERE stream_id=8467 AND event_time > now() - interval '2 hours' AND event_time > processing_time;"
```

eng-runtime-li: If that returns >0, we likely have events where event_time > processing_time (i.e., clocks or processing reorder). Also check aggregator logs for the clamp:```
grep 'computed_tokens_per_sec' /var/log/ingest/aggregator.log | tail -n 200
```

support-jen: Ran the SQL check with customer data (with limited access) — got 17 rows where event_time > processing_time.

eng-runtime-li: That matches. Root cause hypothesis: recent change in ingestion pipeline (PR #3821) tried to optimize by emitting an "end" event from the first flush of an already-closed segment. In certain restart/replay cases the start and end timestamps collapse in the wrong order. Aggregator didn't guard against negative durations.

product-alex: Oof. Is this purely a UI/display issue or are downstream billing/alerts affected?

support-jen: Customer billing unaffected for now, they only use Console for monitoring. But alerts that rely on tokens/sec thresholds could be noisy.

eng-runtime-li: Quick mitigation options:
1) Hotfix: clamp duration to a min of 1ms before dividing (safe, prevents negative).
2) Disable new emitter path by flipping feature flag: streaming_metrics_v2=false and restart aggregator (rollback ingest-emitter).
3) Backfill: detect negative metrics and replay events or reconstruct metrics from raw tokens.

ops-maya: I can flip the feature flag for dedicated-nyc-1 and restart aggregator shards. That should stop new bad rows from arriving.

support-jen: Customer is asking for ETA on fix + temporary workaround. Recommending option 2 now.

eng-runtime-li: I'll prepare a patch for option 1 as it addresses edge case more gracefully. Patch created: https://git.redwood.ai/r/ingest/+/PR-3899 (summary: clamp duration to max(duration, 0.001) and log if negative durations seen). Will run unit tests and deploy to staging in ~30m.

deploy-bot: Rolling change detected: rolling back feature flag streaming_metrics_v2 on cluster dedicated-nyc-1. 6/6 nodes updated.

ops-maya: Flag flipped. After flag flip, Console shows no new negative tokens/sec but historical rows remain.

eng-runtime-li: For backfill, run this small script (careful, dry-run first):

```
python backfill_streaming_metrics.py --stream 8467 --start "2026-04-02T02:00:00Z" --end "2026-04-02T04:00:00Z" --dry-run
```

It reconstructs metrics from raw token events and skips rows where duration <= 0 unless forced. Backfill run on staging succeeded and fixed ~95% of negative rows.

support-jen: Communicated to customer: we rolled back the new emitter on their cluster, preparing a backfill for their window. They're happy with rollback + backfill cadence.

eng-runtime-li: Postmortem action items: 1) add duration clamp and telemetry (PR-3899), 2) add invariant check in ingestion to avoid emitting end < start, 3) add alert for >0 negative-duration metric rows, 4) add automated backfill job for short reorders.

product-alex: Please include messaging for console UI that shows an explanatory tooltip when TTFT is missing: "metric unavailable due to ingestion reordering — retrying backfill" so customers aren't confused.

samir: Thanks all. Summary: rollback feature flag applied, patch PR opened, backfill plan in progress, will follow up when backfill completes. @support-jen please update ticket with timeline. :thumbsup:

support-jen: Will do. Ticket updated and customer notified. Closing thread unless anything else pops up.

eng-runtime-li: One more note for engineers: when reproducing locally, this small repro shows negative tokens/sec quickly:

```
# repro: emit start at t=1000, emit end at t=999, tokens=500
emit_event("start", stream=8467, ts=1000)
emit_event("end", stream=8467, ts=999, tokens=500)
# aggregator will compute tokens_per_sec = 500 / (999-1000) -> -500
```

Patch will make the aggregator treat duration <= 0 as sentinel and log and skip or clamp.

ops-maya: Monitoring shows no new anomalies after rollback. I'll coordinate backfill windows with support-jen and run during low-traffic window.

samir: Good follow-up. Closing.
